answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-stake registry with slashing, enforced by an on-chain verification kernel. Each agent locks a fixed bond, say 1,000 POA, to register in the trellis of active identities, so spinning up 1,000 sybils ties up 1,000,000 POA. Each agent posts heartbeats stamped by a shared quartz-disciplined clock; a missed or forged heartbeat lets the kernel slash that bond. An attacker breaks this only by funding every fake identity with a real, slashable bond, so cheap mass identities stop paying off.
